To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the energy efficiency of an ultra-low power system is limited by the efficiency of the microprocessor and memory, and that ultra-low power sensor systems can be optimized by minimizing the number of clock cycles and the number of accesses to the memory.

the microprocessor, timer, and memory are the three most important components for the design of an ultra-low power node, and that the energy budget is dominated by either microprocessor, timer or memory depending on the application.

the energy budget is dominated by the microprocessor, the memory, and the timer in three distinct scenarios, and the corresponding design guidelines for these three components, respectively, are to use an ultra-low power microprocessor with a small code footprint, to use a low-leakage SRAM memory with an efficient power-down scheme, and to use a timer with a low-leakaging clock generator and an efficient power-down mechanism.
